newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade airport to handle 15,000 tonnes by end-97.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade airport to handle 15,000 tonnes by end-97.

text.p: The Belgrade airport cargo service expects to handle 15,000 tonnes of goods by the end of 1997 after growing an average 20 percent per month since the beginning of the year, Belgrade daily Politika said on Tuesday.

"The Surcin cargo service expects to handle 15,000 tonnes of goods by the end of the year which is half the amount handled in pre-sanctions years," manager of the Belgrade airport cargo service Slobodan Cojic was quoted as saying.
"Business in the cargo service was virtually at a standstill during the sanctions and now it is constantly growing. The trend is 20 percent growth a month," Cojic said.
The United Nations imposed war-related sanctions on Yugoslavia in 1992 and formally lifted them in October 1996.
Cojic said the airport, with its 5,500 square metres of indoor storage space, handled 5,300 tonnes of goods from January to July.
The service includes the reception and forwarding of goods home and abroad, storage, customs control and flight forwarding.
"There is still room now but since turnover is growing considerably the available space will soon become inadequate," said Cojic.

Even before the sanctions the airport planned to extend the storage facility by another 1,000 square metres, Cojic said and added that the international shipper DHL was interested in investing in this project.
The airport also planned to build 900 square metres of new office premises, introduce computers and extend the parking lot. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
